name: Padikasu Nathar Temple, Arisilkaraipudur (Alagaputhur)
deity: Shiva as Padikasu Nathar (Swarnapureeswarar, lord who gave the daily gold coin), with the goddess Soundara Nayaki (Azhagammai)
period: Tevaram era (hymned 7th century); later Chola structural temple
summary: Alagaputhur, also Arisilkaraipudur, near Kumbakonam, honours Shiva as Padikasu Nathar — also Swarnapureeswarar — with the goddess Soundara Nayaki. A Paadal Petra Sthalam hymned by Sambandar, Appar and Sundarar, it is the birthplace of Pugazh Thunai Nayanar, to whom, in a famine, the lord is said to have given a gold coin each day on the temple step — the padikasu that gives the deity his tender name.

sections.history: Alagaputhur, also called Arisilkaraipudur for its situation on the bank of the Arisil river, lies about 6–7 km from Kumbakonam in Thanjavur district. It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam, revered in the Tevaram, with hymns by Tirugnana Sambandar, Appar and Sundarar. The village is cherished as the birthplace of Pugazh Thunai Nayanar, one of the sixty-three Nayanmars, whose story is woven into the temple's own name. The stone temple is of the Chola period and later.
sections.architecture: A Dravidian delta temple, the shrine enshrines Padikasu Nathar — also Swarnapureeswarar, 'the lord of the golden city' — in the sanctum, with the goddess Soundara Nayaki, also Azhagammai, in her own shrine. A Nandi and the parivara devatas complete the plan; the sthala vriksham is the vilva, and the sacred tank is the Amirtha Pushkarini. The temple steps, where the gold coin appeared, are themselves part of its sanctity.
sections.legends: The great legend is that of Pugazh Thunai Nayanar, a poor and devout Shaiva of this village who performed the daily abhishekam of the lord without fail. When a terrible famine came and he grew weak with hunger, Shiva, unwilling to let his devotee's service lapse, placed a single gold coin — a padikasu — on the temple step each day, enough to sustain him and continue the worship. From this grace the lord is praised as Padikasu Nathar, and the name Swarnapureeswarar, lord of the golden city, keeps the memory of that golden mercy.
sections.festivals: The temple keeps Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), the festival of Pugazh Thunai Nayanar, and the regular Pradosha and Karthikai observances. Devotees who honour the sixty-three Nayanmars and the Paadal Petra temples of the Kaveri include Alagaputhur among their pilgrimages.
sections.experience: At Alagaputhur the pilgrim comes to a shrine of pure tenderness, where the lord fed his starving devotee with a daily coin of gold. Before Padikasu Nathar and Soundara Nayaki, standing near the steps where the padikasu appeared, the visitor feels the nearness of a god who would not let devotion fail for want of bread — a small temple rich in one of Shaivism's most beloved stories of grace.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Alagaputhur (Arisilkaraipudur) is about 6–7 km from Kumbakonam in Thanjavur district, on the bank of the Arisil river. Kumbakonam is the nearest major rail head, with local buses and taxis to the village.
